## Boards (40)

<p class="rev-plan">Four cards per design: the whole board, then the numbers block, the diagram order and the two deep dives on their own. On the whole-board card, write before you open.</p>

<details class="rev" data-card="b01-board" data-kind="do">
<summary><span class="rev-head"><span class="rev-tag">BOARD 01 · WHOLE BOARD</span><span class="rev-q">Live AI copilot for 1M body-worn and industrial cameras: write the whole board on paper, scale first.</span></span></summary>
<div class="rev-a">

[0-8 min · Requirements, top-left]{.rev-step}

```text
FR   device opens session, streams video+audio+IMU, gets predictions+alerts back
     phone gets every alert once, also after offline (ack)
     supervisor fleet view: streams, lag, drop rate, open alerts
     quotas per org and device · consent fork to storage, revocable
NFR  alert p95 < 1 s on device, < 2 s on phone · region loss -> back < 60 s
     10^4 -> 10^6 devices, same design, partition by device id
     GPU short -> lower fps before any refusal · alerts at-least-once, dedup by id
OUT  training, phone UI, billing, firmware
```

[8-13 min · Numbers, top-right]{.rev-step}

```text
10^4 dev × 5 fps = 5×10^4 f/s ÷ 500 f/s per GPU = 100 GPU (150-200 w/ headroom); 1M -> 10^4 GPU
in  10^4 × 0.25 MB/s = 2.5 GB/s (2× peak)   out 10^4 × 3 × 200 B = 6 MB/s   (400:1)
retain 20% -> 0.5 GB/s -> 43 TB/day; at 1M 4.3 PB/day -> 100 PB in 23 days
hot  session 200 B × 10^6 = 200 MB · limiter 66 MB · state 2 MB × 10^4 = 20 GB on GPU hosts
alerts 20/dev/day -> 2/s today, 230/s at 1M      ports at 1M: 500 GB/s ÷ 12.5 = 40 × 100 GbE
-> GPUs force it: admission and frame sampling ARE the design; bytes and alerts are ordinary
```

[13-17 min · API, left]{.rev-step}

```text
POST /sessions {device, org, model, retain} -> {session_id, gateway_url, token, granted_fps}  (idempotent per device)
stream up: {seq, ts, frame|audio|imu}   down: {result_seq, type, alert_id, payload} + ctrl {granted_fps}; device acks result_seq
POST /sessions/{id}/resume {token, last_result_seq}  (60 s grace) -> gateway_url
WS /connect (phone) down: {alert_id, device, severity, summary}  up ack {alert_id}
GET /orgs/{o}/fleet?window=5s · PUT /devices/{d}/consent {retain:false}
```

[17-21 min · Data, left under API]{.rev-step}

```text
session(session_id; idx device_id): gateway, gpu_host, granted_fps, retain -> Redis TTL, per region
model state + unacked results (60 s ring)                       -> GPU host memory
counters(org concurrent sessions; device open rate)             -> Redis
alert(alert_id = hash(device, 2 s window, type))                -> Cassandra (org, day, bucket)
inbox(user_id, alert_id, acked, TTL 7 d) · phone_map(user)      -> Cassandra · Redis
metrics -> Kafka -> TSDB · orgs, devices, quotas, consent -> Postgres
```

[21-36 min · Diagram, center, in draw order]{.rev-step}

```text
1 devices -> API gateway (device certs, home region) -> admission (Redis counters) -> session store
2 devices -> stream gateways (decode, sample to granted fps, 10 s ring) -> batcher + deadline -> GPU hosts (state) -> back
3 stream gateway -> alert service -> Cassandra (alert + inbox) -> phone gateways / push -> phones
4 stream gateways -> Kafka (counters every 2 s) -> roll-up per org/site -> TSDB -> supervisor view
5 stream gateways -> object storage (consented segments only)      6 control plane -> admission, gateways
```

[36-52 min · Two deep dives, annotate the boxes]{.rev-step}

```text
A stickiness/resume: gateway = pipe, GPU host = state; session names both · device carries last_result_seq
  host keeps 60 s unacked results -> new gateway resends only those · gateway dies: 3 s heartbeat, 0-5 s jitter, same host, 3-8 s gap
  host dies: replay 10 s ring (50 frames ≈ 0.1 GPU-s) · both: device replays flash · REJECT stateless GWs; state checkpoints (67 GB/s at 1M)
B admission: L1 at open, before GPU state: concurrent-session counter per org + open rate per device; contract in frames/s
  L2 live: controller reads GPU queue age each 1 s -> lower granted_fps by priority tag (fixed low-risk 5->2 first, hazard wearers last)
  floor 1 fps -> 429 for new low-priority only; open sessions never cut · limiter down -> fail-open at last rate · REJECT queueing; arrival order
```

[52-57 min · Failures and trade-offs, bottom]{.rev-step}

```text
gateway dies   -> 3 s heartbeats      -> jittered resume, same host, resend from host   -> 3-8 s without cloud alerts
region lost    -> 10-30 s cross checks -> paired region, device replay, fps down          -> alerts back < 60 s
GPU saturates  -> queue age vs deadline -> fps by priority, 429 new low-prio             -> safety classes unchanged
chose: frames/s quotas over RPS · degrade over refuse · disposable GW + sticky host · replay over checkpoint · event-keyed alert id · GW-side metrics · consent flag at GW
```

[57-60 min · Summary, said not written.]{.rev-step}

"Devices stream to regional gateways, a world model answers within a second, each phone gets each alert once. 5×10^4 frames/s is 100 to 200 GPUs today and 10^4 at a million, so admission in frames per second and degrade-before-refuse are the design; a disposable gateway plus a sticky GPU host makes resume cheap; an event-keyed alert id makes duplicates collapse."

<p class="rev-short">Shorthand used on the boards: WS = WebSocket · GW = gateway · KV = key-value store · TTL = time to live · idem = idempotency key · SSE = server-sent events · DLQ = dead-letter queue · P2P = peer-to-peer · 2PC = two-phase commit · CDC = change data capture · WFQ = weighted fair queuing · LWW = last-writer-wins register · HLC = hybrid logical clock · OT = operational transformation · RRF = reciprocal rank fusion · SFU = selective forwarding unit (the media server) · RTCP = the RTP control channel that reports media health · EC = erasure coding · AFR = annual disk failure rate · IOPS = disk operations per second · PFS = parallel file system · TSDB = time-series database.</p>

<p class="rev-actions"><button type="button" class="rev-drawn" data-for="b01-board">drawn today</button></p>

</div>
</details>

<details class="rev" data-card="b02-board" data-kind="do">
<summary><span class="rev-head"><span class="rev-tag">BOARD 02 · WHOLE BOARD</span><span class="rev-q">The multimodal AI API platform: write the whole board on paper, scale first.</span></span></summary>
<div class="rev-a">

[0-8 min · Requirements, top-left]{.rev-step}

```text
FR   sync infer (image + text -> answer, optional token stream) · stream session (video in, results out, resume)
     async job (hours of video -> poll/webhook, partial results) · keys, tiers, quotas -> 429 + Retry-After
     usage per key, dashboard, monthly invoice · aliases, pinned versions, canary, rollback, deprecation
NFR  sync p95 < 2 s, first token < 1 s · stream result < 500 ms · gateway < 20 ms
     every billable event in the ledger exactly once · a 100× flooder moves others' p95 < 10% · rollback < 1 min
OUT  model internals, card payments, portal UI, moderation policy
```

[8-13 min · Numbers, top-right]{.rev-step}

```text
10^9/day ÷ 86,400 ≈ 11,600/s -> ×3 peak ≈ 35,000/s
sync  0.95 × 35k ≈ 33k/s ÷ 20 calls/s per GPU ≈ 1,650 GPU  <- the bill
stream 10^4 × 5 fps = 5×10^4 f/s ÷ 500 ≈ 100-200 GPU (frame ≈ 60 tokens via streaming encoder, 1/25 of an image)
jobs  10^4 h × 3,600 f ÷ 86,400 ≈ 420 f/s ≈ 1 GPU        total ≈ 2,000 GPU
in ≈ 5 GB/s (2.2 sync + 2.5 stream + 0.1 jobs) · out ≈ 22 MB/s · usage events 10^9 × 200 B = 200 GB/day
-> 35k rps is a small gateway problem; 2,000 GPUs is the cost -> count tokens and GPU-seconds, never requests
```

[13-17 min · API, left]{.rev-step}

```text
POST /infer  {model: alias|version, content: [{image file_id}, {text}], max_tokens, stream}  + Idempotency-Key
             -> {id, model_version, content, usage {in, out, gpu_ms}, decision_id}   SSE deltas when stream=true
POST /files -> presigned URL + file_id
POST /sessions {model} -> {session_id, stream_url, token} · POST /sessions/{id}/resume {last_result_seq}
POST /jobs {file_ids, model, callback_url} + Idempotency-Key -> 202 {job_id} · GET /jobs/{id} · /results?cursor
GET  /usage?key&from&to&granularity=hour
```

[17-21 min · Data, left under API]{.rev-step}

```text
key(key_hash): tenant, tier, status               -> Postgres, copied to gateway RAM
limiter(tenant + window; key sub-limit)           -> Redis, TTL 2× window
idem(tenant, idempotency_key) -> response hash/ptr -> Postgres UNIQUE (Redis fast path); bodies -> object store
session(session_id): pinned host, last_result_seq -> Redis TTL, 60 s grace
job(job_id) / chunk(job_id, n) state machine      -> Postgres; inputs and partial results -> object store
usage_event(event_id) -> Kafka by tenant -> Parquet · ledger(key, version, hour, revision) -> Postgres double-entry
routing policy (alias -> version, weight) · decision log(request_id)
```

[21-36 min · Diagram, center, in draw order]{.rev-step}

```text
1 apps -> API gateway (key auth, token limiter in Redis, idempotency) 
2 gateway -> model router (alias -> version + pool, 1 s capacity view) -> fair-share queues (tier, key) -> sync GPU pools
3 gateway -> session router (hash session_id, session map) -> streaming pool (pinned hosts) <-> apps
4 gateway -> job queue -> job workers (chunk, checkpoint) -> object store; workers -> same admission queues at lowest weight; DLQ; webhook sender
5 all pools -> Kafka usage topic -> aggregator (dedup) -> ledger -> invoices/dashboard; Kafka -> raw Parquet
6 control plane (keys, tiers, registry, rollout) -> gateway, router
```

[36-52 min · Two deep dives, annotate the boxes]{.rev-step}

```text
A fair share: bucket per TENANT in tokens/min + concurrency, key sub-limits · admission cost = counted input + max_tokens, refund after
  weighted fair queues per tier 5/3/1, Enterprise reserved pool · round-robin per key + queue cap · deadline -> fast 429/503, Free shed first
  jobs at lowest weight, yield at chunk boundary · REJECT rps-only limits (1 h video = 10 tokens); strict priority (Free starves)
B metering: one id gateway -> meter -> ledger (request_id = hash(tenant, idem key)) · emit where the work ran (sync per request, stream per 10 s, job per chunk)
  Kafka at-least-once; dedup set covers 7 d retention (112 GB over 256 partitions), commits with offsets · sum per (key, version, hour)
  ledger insert UNIQUE aggregate_id · late event -> revision row, never an edit · nightly raw Parquet vs ledger -> page on mismatch
  REJECT count at gateway (bills failed calls, never sees GPU time); balance row per request (35k hot writes/s)
```

[52-57 min · Failures and trade-offs, bottom]{.rev-step}

```text
tenant floods 100×  -> 429 rate per key        -> BLOCKED flag 1 s in gateway RAM, per-key queue cap   -> others see nothing
version regresses   -> per-version p99 + judge -> freeze canary, alias back to v1 (resident)          -> minutes of slow answers for canary keys
metering lags       -> consumer lag, hour late -> 7 d retention, scale aggregators, invoices wait     -> dashboard late, bills late never wrong
chose: one gateway for 3 shapes · tokens/GPU-s per tenant · WFQ over strict priority · one id + idempotent sink · hourly ledger · session map · alias + resident old version
```

[57-60 min · Summary, said not written.]{.rev-step}

"One gateway and one key model for three shapes. 35k requests a second is small; 2,000 GPUs is the bill, so I limit and share in tokens and GPU-seconds per tenant with weighted fair queues, carry one id from the gateway into a double-entry ledger so a retry is never billed twice, and route aliases with canaries per key and rollback by policy."

<p class="rev-short">Shorthand used on the boards: WS = WebSocket · GW = gateway · KV = key-value store · TTL = time to live · idem = idempotency key · SSE = server-sent events · DLQ = dead-letter queue · P2P = peer-to-peer · 2PC = two-phase commit · CDC = change data capture · WFQ = weighted fair queuing · LWW = last-writer-wins register · HLC = hybrid logical clock · OT = operational transformation · RRF = reciprocal rank fusion · SFU = selective forwarding unit (the media server) · RTCP = the RTP control channel that reports media health · EC = erasure coding · AFR = annual disk failure rate · IOPS = disk operations per second · PFS = parallel file system · TSDB = time-series database.</p>

<p class="rev-actions"><button type="button" class="rev-drawn" data-for="b02-board">drawn today</button></p>

</div>
</details>

<details class="rev" data-card="b03-board" data-kind="do">
<summary><span class="rev-head"><span class="rev-tag">BOARD 03 · WHOLE BOARD</span><span class="rev-q">Petabyte video lake feeding a 1,000-GPU training cluster: write the whole board on paper, scale first.</span></span></summary>
<div class="rev-a">

[0-8 min · Requirements, top-left]{.rev-step}

```text
FR   ingest device streams + licensed footage; originals immutable · transcode to training renditions, 3 MB shards
     dataset = filter over catalog -> frozen immutable manifest · pre-stage a job's shards to cluster NVMe; read at line rate
     detect disk loss, rebuild, report degraded/lost objects · consent revoke -> delete originals, exclude from new versions
NFR  11 nines/object/yr for originals (renditions rebuildable) · 200 GB/s sustained, GPU data-wait < 1%
     ingest 1.4 GB/s, 2× peak · manifest lookup p99 < 10 ms · rebuild one disk < 2 h · a running job never sees input change
OUT  training code, labeling, embedding search, human playback
```

[8-13 min · Numbers, top-right]{.rev-step}

```text
100 PB × 12/9 = 133 PB raw ÷ 20 TB = 6,700 HDD (+5% spare) in ~110 chassis of 60 · renditions 25 PB -> own pool, ~1,700 disks
objects 100 PB ÷ 1 GB = 10^8 · segments 100 PB ÷ 3 MB = 3.3×10^10 · manifests 10^8 × 10 KB = 1 TB
reads 1,000 GPU × 200 MB/s = 200 GB/s ÷ 3 MB = 6.7×10^4 reads/s  vs  6,700 × 40 IOPS = 2.7×10^5 -> only 4× headroom
NVMe 125 nodes × 4 × 8 TB = 4 PB, 1.5 TB/s · hot set 5 datasets × 500 TB = 2.5 PB (63%) · stage 500 TB at 50 GB/s = 2.8 h
rebuild 20 TB: 1 disk 28 h; declustered floor 3 GB/s -> 1.9 h (27 GB/s reads = 3% of IOPS) · ingest 42-44 PB/yr = 2,800 disks/yr
-> IOPS forces it: 4× headroom only while healthy -> jobs read staged NVMe; HDDs see staging, misses, repair
```

[13-17 min · API, left]{.rev-step}

```text
POST /:bucket/:obj?uploads -> upload_id · PUT ?upload_id&part=N (3 MB, idempotent) · POST complete {parts, checksums} -> READY
POST /datasets {filter} -> dataset_id · POST /datasets/{id}/versions -> 202 {version, manifest_ref, shards, bytes}
POST /stagings {dataset, version, job_id, deadline} -> 202 · GET /stagings/{id} -> {bytes_staged, bytes_total}
GET  /shards/{id} -> 3 MB (loader lib: local NVMe first, store on miss) · GET /incidents/{disk_id} -> degraded/lost
```

[17-21 min · Data, left under API]{.rev-step}

```text
manifest(bucket, object): segments, checksums, 12 chunk locations/stripe -> KV, 3 replicas, quorum (write-once)
disk_index(disk_id) -> chunks held                                          -> same KV (rebuild w/o scanning manifests)
stripe_state(stripe_id): chunks alive, repair priority                     -> Raft-replicated (changes during repair)
catalog(object_id): device, org, consent, time, labels, clip ranges        -> Parquet + query engine
dataset_version(dataset, v): sorted shard ids (2.7 GB per 500 TB)           -> object store, immutable
staging_map(version, shard) -> node                                          -> stager KV, rebuildable
```

[21-36 min · Diagram, center, in draw order]{.rev-step}

```text
1 board 1 gateways + licensed footage -> ingest API (multipart) -> placement + EC 9+3 (one 3 MB chunk per disk) -> HDD store
2 placement -> manifest KV, disk index · ingest "ready" -> Kafka -> transcode workers -> renditions -> placement; attributes -> catalog
3 researchers -> dataset service (filter -> frozen manifest) -> manifests store
4 job scheduler -> stager (throttled prefetch) -> HDD store -> cluster NVMe (4 PB) <- data loaders (1,000 GPUs); miss -> HDD
5 repair service (priority by redundancy left) -> disk index, HDD · scrubber -> HDD
```

[36-52 min · Two deep dives, annotate the boxes]{.rev-step}

```text
A EC layout + rebuild: stripe = 9 consecutive segments of ONE object + 3 parity, 12 disks in 12 chassis; 37 stripes per 1 GB object
  read touches 1 disk; parity only on failure · delete frees whole stripes (consent) · declustered: all disks rebuild in parallel
  loss/stripe/yr ≈ 12·AFR·C(11,3)·p³, p = AFR·T/8,760: AFR 5%, T 28 h -> 4×10⁻¹⁰/stripe -> ×37 = 1.5×10⁻⁸/object (7.8 nines)
  T 1.9 h (3 GB/s floor) -> 1.3×10⁻¹³/stripe -> 5×10⁻¹²/object = 11 nines · loss ∝ T³ · fallback 9+4 = 14 nines at 44% overhead
  REJECT 3× replication (15,000 disks); striping a segment over 9 disks (6×10⁵ reads/s > 2.7×10⁵); mixed-object stripes (deletion re-encodes)
B staging tier: job queue = demand forecast (Netflix at night) · stager copies next job's manifest to NVMe at ≤ 50 GB/s
  keyed by shard id -> overlapping datasets share bytes; refcount pins running + next; LRU on unpinned · start gate = first epoch staged
  misses read through; loader prefetch buffer absorbs · lost node: refetch 32 TB at 5 GB/s < 2 h · REJECT pull cache (cold epoch vs HDD IOPS); second PFS
```

[52-57 min · Failures and trade-offs, bottom]{.rev-step}

```text
disk dies daily      -> loader errors, scrubber -> degraded reads 9 of 11, rebuild 1.9 h from disk index -> nothing (jobs read NVMe)
2 disks same stripes -> stripe state = 2 missing -> those ~11,000 stripes first (66 GB at 3 GB/s ≈ 20 s)   -> nothing
manifest replica dies-> quorum health          -> 2 of 3 serve, rebuild from peers, loaders keep cached manifests -> nothing
chose: 9+3 one chunk per disk over 3× · whole segment over striping · per-object stripes · declustered 3 GB/s floor · pre-stage over pull · disposable NVMe · immutable manifests · clips as ranges, packed on freeze
```

[57-60 min · Summary, said not written.]{.rev-step}

"A 100 PB immutable lake feeding 1,000 GPUs at 200 GB/s. IOPS is the forcing number: 6,700 disks for capacity but only 4× read headroom, so jobs read pre-staged NVMe and the HDDs see staging, misses and repair. One 3 MB chunk per disk in 9+3 stripes that never mix objects, declustered rebuild at a 3 GB/s floor for 11 nines, and immutable manifests so a running job never sees its input change."

<p class="rev-short">Shorthand used on the boards: WS = WebSocket · GW = gateway · KV = key-value store · TTL = time to live · idem = idempotency key · SSE = server-sent events · DLQ = dead-letter queue · P2P = peer-to-peer · 2PC = two-phase commit · CDC = change data capture · WFQ = weighted fair queuing · LWW = last-writer-wins register · HLC = hybrid logical clock · OT = operational transformation · RRF = reciprocal rank fusion · SFU = selective forwarding unit (the media server) · RTCP = the RTP control channel that reports media health · EC = erasure coding · AFR = annual disk failure rate · IOPS = disk operations per second · PFS = parallel file system · TSDB = time-series database.</p>

rebuild 20 TB: 1 disk 28 h; declustered floor 3 GB/s -> 1.9 h (27 GB/s reads = 3% of IOPS) · ingest 42-44 PB/yr = 2,800 disks/yr

<details class="rev" data-card="b04-board" data-kind="do">
<summary><span class="rev-head"><span class="rev-tag">BOARD 04 · WHOLE BOARD</span><span class="rev-q">The training factory: schedule, checkpoint, evaluate, ship (the infra spine): write the whole board on paper, scale first.</span></span></summary>
<div class="rev-a">

[0-8 min · Requirements, top-left]{.rev-step}

```text
FR   submit/cancel/watch train + eval jobs, one-off or nightly · gang: all GPUs or none, within team quota + priority
     preempt lower priority (checkpoint before kill), backfill · auto checkpoint/resume after node failure
     registry: immutable artifact + lineage (data manifest, commit, config) · promote through eval gates, roll out per region, auto-rollback
NFR  never two leaders / zero double-allocated GPUs (fencing) · scheduler failover < 30 s, running jobs unaffected
     work lost/failure avg 25 min, max 40 · checkpoint stall < 2 min (target 30 s) · goodput > 94% · rollback < 1 min
OUT  training code + parallelism, object store internals (board 3), serving data plane (board 2), chargeback
```

[8-13 min · Numbers, top-right]{.rev-step}

```text
125 nodes × 8 = 1,000 GPU; flagship 960 GPU on 120 nodes + 5 hot spares · 2,000 jobs/day = 0.02/s · heartbeats 12.5/s -> control plane idle
70B fp16 = 140 GB; ×4 optimizer = 560 GB/checkpoint (≈ 1 TB with fp32 master weights) · every 30 min, keep 10 -> 5.6 TB/job
sync to store in 2 min = 4.7 GB/s burst ✗ · per node 560 ÷ 120 = 4.7 GB -> NVMe 1.6 s + peer copy < 1 s ✓ · drain 1.5 GB/s -> durable in 6 min
work lost = 960 × (15 + 10 restart) min ÷ 60 ≈ 400 GPU-h × 2/day ≈ 3.5% · Young: √(2 × 0.5 min × 720 min MTBF) ≈ 27 min -> 30 min
rollout 250 hosts × 140 GB = 35 TB; origin 10 GB/s -> 1 h -> P2P
-> 400 GPU-h per failure vs a 560 GB checkpoint forces: local commit in seconds, async drain, cadence from failure rate
```

[13-17 min · API, left]{.rev-step}

```text
POST /jobs {team, priority, gpus, image_digest, dataset_manifest_id, config, max_runtime, preemptible, idempotency_key} -> 201 {job_id, QUEUED}
GET  /jobs/{id}/events?stream (SSE): QUEUED RESERVING RUNNING CHECKPOINTING PREEMPTED RESTARTING SUCCEEDED FAILED
POST /schedules {cron, job_template, missed_run_policy: run_late_within_4h|skip}
POST /models/{name}/versions {checkpoint_uri, sha256, lineage} -> {version_id} (same digest -> same version)
POST /rollouts {model, version, regions, steps [1,10,50,100], gates {p99, error, eval}} -> 202 · POST /rollouts/{id}/rollback
```

[17-21 min · Data, left under API]{.rev-step}

```text
job(job_id) state machine, quota sums per team          -> Postgres
allocation(node, gpu) -> job, written with epoch check   -> Postgres (1 row per GPU = double booking is a constraint violation)
scheduler_epoch (single row, fencing token)             -> Postgres, SELECT FOR UPDATE in every allocation tx
leader lease · node leases (10 s KeepAlive, 20 s TTL)   -> lock service, 5-node consensus
checkpoint_manifest(job, step): LOCAL_COMMITTED|DURABLE, shards, checksums, holders -> Postgres; shards -> NVMe (writer + peer) -> object store
model_version(model, id) + lineage -> Postgres; blob by sha256 -> object store · rollout(rollout_id, region, step) -> Postgres
```

[21-36 min · Diagram, center, in draw order]{.rev-step}

```text
1 researchers/CLI -> job API (idempotent) -> Postgres (jobs, allocations, registry) · nightly trigger -> job API
2 lock service -> scheduler leader (gang, quota, preempt, backfill) -> Postgres · leader -> node agents ×125 (lease 10 s) -> lock service
3 agents -> local NVMe (writer + peer) -> object store (drain) -> registry (immutable versions)
4 registry -> eval gates (64-GPU jobs via job API) -> rollout controller (canary per region) -> serving fleet (P2P pull) -> metrics -> controller
```

[36-52 min · Two deep dives, annotate the boxes]{.rev-step}

```text
A gang + preempt: queues per team by deficit vs quota; prod > research > backfill · reserve N GPUs in one island -> commit all or release all, 60 s timeout
  every allocation tx locks epoch row, compares fencing token, aborts if lower · preempt: fewest lowest-priority victims freeing an island, "checkpoint now", 5 min grace, kill
  backfill jobs with max_runtime < time to next big reservation · anti-starvation: big job waiting > 2 h gets a reservation
  REJECT pod-by-pod K8s (two 512 jobs each hold 400 forever); optimistic multi-scheduler (half-cluster jobs conflict with everything)
B checkpoint path: GPU -> pinned host RAM (only stall) -> NVMe 1.6 s + peer NVMe -> LOCAL_COMMITTED ~10 s -> drain 1.5 GB/s -> DURABLE ~6 min
  cadence Young √(2·cost·MTBF) = 27 -> 30 min · manifest lists shards+checksums+holders; partial step never resumed · resume from newest LOCAL_COMMITTED with live holders, else DURABLE
  reshard on resume · keep 10 + milestones, GC after manifest expired · REJECT sync write to store (4.7 GB/s, slowest shard stalls all); PFS sized for burst (idle 28/30 min)
```

[52-57 min · Failures and trade-offs, bottom]{.rev-step}

```text
node dies mid-step  -> lease 20 s + agent aborts collectives -> spare node, restart from LOCAL_COMMITTED -> RESTARTING, ≤ 30 + 10 min lost
leader dies/pauses  -> session TTL 20 s, standby takes lock 1 s -> reads Postgres; stale writes fail epoch check -> queue waits ~21 s, jobs unaffected
rollout degrades p99-> gate breach 2 min vs OLD version   -> flip pointer back (old resident), freeze, page  -> minutes of higher p99 for 1-10%
chose: reserve->commit over pod-by-pod · one leader + epoch fencing · cadence from failure rate · LOCAL_COMMITTED then DURABLE · 960 + 5 spares · content-addressed versions, pointer flip · P2P weights
```

[57-60 min · Summary, said not written.]{.rev-step}

"The control plane of a 1,000-GPU cluster growing to 10,000. A 560 GB checkpoint and 400 GPU-hours per failure twice a day force the design: one leader with fencing on every allocation and reserve-then-commit gangs so no GPU is booked twice; checkpoints committed on writer plus peer NVMe in seconds with an async drain so the recovery point is fresh; immutable versions rolled out by pointer flip with the old version resident."

<p class="rev-short">Shorthand used on the boards: WS = WebSocket · GW = gateway · KV = key-value store · TTL = time to live · idem = idempotency key · SSE = server-sent events · DLQ = dead-letter queue · P2P = peer-to-peer · 2PC = two-phase commit · CDC = change data capture · WFQ = weighted fair queuing · LWW = last-writer-wins register · HLC = hybrid logical clock · OT = operational transformation · RRF = reciprocal rank fusion · SFU = selective forwarding unit (the media server) · RTCP = the RTP control channel that reports media health · EC = erasure coding · AFR = annual disk failure rate · IOPS = disk operations per second · PFS = parallel file system · TSDB = time-series database.</p>

<details class="rev" data-card="b05-board" data-kind="do">
<summary><span class="rev-head"><span class="rev-tag">BOARD 05 · WHOLE BOARD</span><span class="rev-q">Collaborative AI video workspace for organizations (people working together, with AI participants): write the whole board on paper, scale first.</span></span></summary>
<div class="rev-a">

[0-8 min · Requirements, top-left]{.rev-step}

```text
FR   orgs, roles, SSO, audit · live video room ≤ 50 (WebRTC), recording · shared canvas + notes that converge (offline too)
     room chat, opened read-only to thousands · presence + cursors · AI assistants join as participants (transcribe, summarize, detect, answer)
NFR  media < 300 ms glass-to-glass · state/cursors < 100 ms · chat < 200 ms · AI events < 1 s
     removed user loses every plane < 1 s · zero lost acked edits; viewer chat may shed, history may not · media failure never stops editing · AI cost per org bounded
OUT  the model/serving (board 2), codec/SFU internals, billing, mobile push
```

[8-13 min · Numbers, top-right]{.rev-step}

```text
50k rooms × 8 = 400k participants + 50 big rooms × 2k = 100k viewers -> 500k sockets
media 400k × 7 receivers × 1 Mbps = 2.8 Tbps ≈ 350 GB/s ÷ 5 Gbps/SFU (CPU-bound) = 560 -> ~700 SFUs · 50-room worst 50×49×1 = 2.45 Gbps -> cap 9 tiles -> 225 Mbps
state 50k × 80 msg/s = 4M/s in, ×7 = 28M/s raw -> batch 100 ms -> 500k × 10 = 5M/s ÷ 10^5 per gateway = 50 -> plan 100 (5k sockets each)
AI 10k sessions × 5 fps = 50k f/s ÷ 500 = 100-200 GPU · room state 0.6 MB × 50k = 30 GB · op log ~14 TB/day · snapshots 500 MB/s · recordings 45 TB/day
-> 2.8 Tbps vs 5M frames/s: two planes on different servers, media sized by CPU, state by frames per second
```

[13-17 min · API, left]{.rev-step}

```text
POST /rooms {org, mode: meeting|broadcast, recording, assistants[]} + idempotency_key -> 201 {room_id}
POST /rooms/{id}/join -> {sfu_url, ice, media_token, state_ws_url, state_token, snapshot_url, snapshot_seq}  (tokens expire in 60 s and carry perm_version, the permission version they were issued under)
WS up: {op_id: client+counter, doc: canvas|notes, update: CRDT bytes}   down: every 100 ms {seq_from, seq_to, updates, cursors, presence}; reconnect {last_seq}
POST /rooms/{id}/messages {client_nonce, text} -> {message_id (Snowflake)}   (REST send, WS receive, as Discord)
POST /rooms/{id}/assistants {assistant, scopes [media:video, canvas:suggest, chat:post], fps} -> {participant_id} · 429 when org AI quota spent
```

[17-21 min · Data, left under API]{.rev-step}

```text
org, user, role, membership                         -> Postgres
permission snapshot(room:user, perm_version)        -> Redis, deleted on role event
room directory(room_id -> room server, SFU, epoch)   -> Redis 10 s lease; epoch bumped on reassignment (fencing)
canvas/notes snapshot(room, doc, seq)               -> object store (600 KB, every 60 s or 5,000 ops)
CRDT update log(room, doc, seq)                     -> Kafka -> Cassandra · chat(room + day, Snowflake) -> ScyllaDB
audit(org, ts) -> Kafka -> write-once object store · recordings(org/room/segment) -> object store
```

[21-36 min · Diagram, center, in draw order]{.rev-step}

```text
1 clients <-> SFU cluster (media plane, ~700)      2 clients <-> WS gateways (state plane, ~100) <-> room servers (CRDT merge, chat order, sticky by room+epoch)
3 clients -> API gateway (SSO, JWT, org rate limits) -> room servers   4 room servers -> pub/sub per room -> viewer gateways (shed, batch)
5 room servers -> Kafka (ops, chat, audit) -> stores        6 SFU -> AI workers (bot peers) <-> AI platform (board 2); AI workers -> WS (suggestion layer)
7 identity service -> WS gateways, room servers, SFUs (revocations)    8 SFU -> recorder -> object store; SFU -> live packager -> CDN (viewers)
```

[36-52 min · Two deep dives, annotate the boxes]{.rev-step}

```text
A editing consistency: canvas = CRDT map shape_id -> per-property LWW registers (HLC + client id); move and recolor both survive; delete beats concurrent move; tombstones to snapshot
  notes = sequence CRDT (Y.js style), unique id per insert · room server relays + assigns delivery seq for resume; correctness never depends on its order
  offline: client keeps state + unacked ops, sends state vector on reconnect, both merge · AI writes suggestion layer only; human accept -> human op
  chat is NOT a CRDT: Snowflake id per room · REJECT central OT (every op needs server, hours offline transform badly); whole-object LWW (loses one of two edits)
B large-room fan-out: ≤ 50 participants direct; viewers read-only behind relay · room server publishes once -> topic -> viewer gateways -> own sockets (one RPC per gateway)
  shed above 50 msg/s to ~10/s per viewer; Kafka/Scylla keep 100% · never shed host/moderator/AI summary; reactions -> counts · slow client: drop oldest queued
  late joiners: snapshot URL + AI summary of last 10 min · perm_version on each socket, recheck on next message · viewers' media = CDN, never SFU
  REJECT room server writes every socket (10⁶ sends/s from one process); polling (10⁴ req/s per room, seconds late)
```

[52-57 min · Failures and trade-offs, bottom]{.rev-step}

```text
SFU dies        -> 3 s RTCP silence -> fence old SFU (epoch), standby SFU, new URL over WS, renegotiate 1-2 s -> video freezes 4-6 s, chat/canvas fine
WS gateway dies -> ~5k sockets drop   -> reconnect 0-5 s jitter with last_seq; room server lease lapses, epoch bump, load snapshot+log -> banner seconds, no lost edits
AI slow         -> result p95 > 2 s, 429s -> breaker, drop late frames, 5 -> 1 fps, "delayed" status -> captions late/sparser, humans unaffected
chose: separate media/state planes · CRDT over OT · per-property registers · Snowflake for chat · relay tree + shedding · AI as bot peer with scopes · push revocation + 60 s tokens · snapshots on time not on ops
```

[57-60 min · Summary, said not written.]{.rev-step}

"Teams watch video, draw, write and chat with AI participants in 50,000 rooms. 2.8 Tbps of media against 5 million state frames a second means two planes sized separately. Per-property CRDT registers for the canvas, a sequence CRDT for notes and AI edits in a suggestion layer keep three kinds of writer converging; a relay tree with shedding serves large rooms while history keeps every message; AI participants are bot peers under per-org quotas."

<p class="rev-short">Shorthand used on the boards: WS = WebSocket · GW = gateway · KV = key-value store · TTL = time to live · idem = idempotency key · SSE = server-sent events · DLQ = dead-letter queue · P2P = peer-to-peer · 2PC = two-phase commit · CDC = change data capture · WFQ = weighted fair queuing · LWW = last-writer-wins register · HLC = hybrid logical clock · OT = operational transformation · RRF = reciprocal rank fusion · SFU = selective forwarding unit (the media server) · RTCP = the RTP control channel that reports media health · EC = erasure coding · AFR = annual disk failure rate · IOPS = disk operations per second · PFS = parallel file system · TSDB = time-series database.</p>

```text
1 clients <-> SFU cluster (media plane, ~700)      2 clients <-> WS gateways (state plane, ~100) <-> room servers (CRDT merge, chat order, sticky by room+epoch)
3 clients -> API gateway (SSO, JWT, org rate limits) -> room servers   4 room servers -> pub/sub per room -> viewer gateways (shed, batch)
5 room servers -> Kafka (ops, chat, audit) -> stores        6 SFU -> AI workers (bot peers) <-> AI platform (board 2); AI workers -> WS (suggestion layer)
7 identity service -> WS gateways, room servers, SFUs (revocations)    8 SFU -> recorder -> object store; SFU -> live packager -> CDN (viewers)
```

<details class="rev" data-card="b05-deepdives" data-kind="say">
<summary><span class="rev-head"><span class="rev-tag">BOARD 05 · DEEP DIVES</span><span class="rev-q">Collaborative AI video workspace for organizations (people working together, with AI participants): the two deep dives (36-52 min).</span></span></summary>
<div class="rev-a">

```text
A editing consistency: canvas = CRDT map shape_id -> per-property LWW registers (HLC + client id); move and recolor both survive; delete beats concurrent move; tombstones to snapshot
  notes = sequence CRDT (Y.js style), unique id per insert · room server relays + assigns delivery seq for resume; correctness never depends on its order
  offline: client keeps state + unacked ops, sends state vector on reconnect, both merge · AI writes suggestion layer only; human accept -> human op
  chat is NOT a CRDT: Snowflake id per room · REJECT central OT (every op needs server, hours offline transform badly); whole-object LWW (loses one of two edits)
B large-room fan-out: ≤ 50 participants direct; viewers read-only behind relay · room server publishes once -> topic -> viewer gateways -> own sockets (one RPC per gateway)
  shed above 50 msg/s to ~10/s per viewer; Kafka/Scylla keep 100% · never shed host/moderator/AI summary; reactions -> counts · slow client: drop oldest queued
  late joiners: snapshot URL + AI summary of last 10 min · perm_version on each socket, recheck on next message · viewers' media = CDN, never SFU
  REJECT room server writes every socket (10⁶ sends/s from one process); polling (10⁴ req/s per room, seconds late)
```

<details class="rev" data-card="b06-board" data-kind="do">
<summary><span class="rev-head"><span class="rev-tag">BOARD 06 · WHOLE BOARD</span><span class="rev-q">Find anything in a billion clips: search, suggest, label (the retrieval spine): write the whole board on paper, scale first.</span></span></summary>
<div class="rev-a">

[0-8 min · Requirements, top-left]{.rev-step}

```text
FR   search by text, by example clip, by metadata (org, device, time) · hybrid ranking over embeddings + labels with filters
     new footage searchable in minutes, new labels within an hour · typeahead over tags/entities
     auto-labels (model) + human review, label versions · datasets = immutable manifests over one label version
NFR  search p99 < 500 ms · typeahead < 100 ms · freshness 5 min clips / 1 h labels · recall@50 ≥ 95% vs exact, nightly
     tenant isolation enforced inside every shard · 99.9%, partial results beat none
OUT  the lake (board 3), training the embedder, annotation UI, billing
```

[8-13 min · Numbers, top-right]{.rev-step}

```text
10⁹ clips × (1,024 dims × 2 B + 256 B HNSW links) = 2.3 KB -> 2.3 TB in RAM -> 16 shards (144 GB each, grow to 300 GB) × 3 replicas = 48 hosts
1,000 QPS × 16 shards = 16k shard searches/s; 30 ms/core -> 32 cores ≈ 1,000/s per host -> 16 hosts per replica set
ingest 10⁷/day ÷ 86,400 ≈ 116 clips/s ÷ 100/GPU ≈ 2 embed GPUs (plan 4) · +23 GB/day index -> 4.6B clips in a year
labels 10⁹ × 20 × 4 B = 80 GB · filter columns 16 GB · metadata 10⁹ × 500 B = 500 GB KV · results 16 × 1.2 KB = 19 KB/query
-> 2.3 TB of vectors in RAM forces 16 shards and a scatter-gather on every query: tail latency and filter handling are the design
```

[13-17 min · API, left]{.rev-step}

```text
POST /search {query: text|example_clip_id, filters {device_ids, time, labels}, k, index_version, cursor} -> {results [{clip_id, score, labels, thumb}], label_version, partial}
     (org_id from token, never the body)
GET  /suggest?prefix=fork -> {suggestions [{text, kind, count}]}  (client debounce 100 ms)
POST /clips/{id}/labels {label, source: model|human, model_version, supersedes, idempotency_key} -> {label_event_id, label_version}
POST /datasets {name, filter, label_as_of} -> 202 {dataset_version_id}
POST /index-builds {embedding_model} -> 202 · PUT /index-aliases/prod {build_id}  (flip; second flip = rollback)
```

[17-21 min · Data, left under API]{.rev-step}

```text
clip metadata(clip_id; idx org+time)            -> KV, p99 < 10 ms (hydration)
vectors(clip_id, model)                         -> object store, columnar = source of truth; every index rebuilt from it
ANN segments(shard, segment, index_version)     -> RAM on shard hosts; files on object store (immutable, swap as units)
label postings(term -> clip_ids) per shard · filter bitmaps(org, day) per shard -> same shard hosts
label events(clip_id, label_event_id)           -> Kafka -> Cassandra (append-only)
dataset manifest(version) -> object store + Postgres row · result cache(hash(query, filters, version), TTL 60 s) -> distributed cache · trie snapshot -> suggest RAM
```

[21-36 min · Diagram, center, in draw order]{.rev-step}

```text
1 video lake (new clip events) -> embed + auto-label GPU workers -> Kafka (vectors, labels by shard) + object store (vectors) · human review -> Kafka
2 Kafka -> 16 shard groups × 3 replicas (immutable segments + delta index) <- merge scheduler (6 h, tiered compaction)
3 client -> API gateway (token -> org) -> query service (parse, encode 20 ms, plan by selectivity) -> result cache -> scatter to 16 shards -> merge -> re-ranker (top 200, GPU) -> metadata KV (top 50)
4 client -> suggest servers (trie in RAM) <- streaming counts <- query logs      5 Kafka -> dataset builder -> manifests
```

[36-52 min · Two deep dives, annotate the boxes]{.rev-step}

```text
A sharding + filters: shard by hash(clip_id) = document-partitioned (Search); each shard a full 62M-clip index with org/day bitmaps -> planner reads counts
  > 10% of shard: HNSW then post-filter, over-fetch k/selectivity · 1-10%: filtered traversal (admit only matching ids, wider beam) · < 1%: skip graph, exact scan (625k × 1,024 ≈ 64 ms/core, 8 ms on 8 cores; 0.01% -> < 1 ms)
  shards return RAW cosine + RAW label score (global IDF), never fused ranks -> query service merges each list, fuses once (RRF) · nightly recall@50 per plan
  REJECT post-filter only (0.01% needs 10,000× over-fetch); partition by vector cluster (hot clusters, filtered recall drops)
B freshness: immutable segments + one small mutable delta HNSW per shard; query reads both · new vector -> shard's Kafka partition -> every replica inserts to delta (< 5 min)
  1.4 GB/shard/day -> merge every 6 h off to the side, tiered compaction keeps < 10 segments; swap atomic, double-buffered; merges on one replica at a time (2× headroom left)
  labels: postings updated in minutes, each carries label_version; results return it · deletes: tombstone bitmap at query time · REJECT nightly rebuild (24 h stale); in-place inserts into big graph
```

[52-57 min · Failures and trade-offs, bottom]{.rev-step}

```text
shard host dies   -> no reply by hedge deadline -> hedge to replica; rebuild from segment files + Kafka offset -> nothing or one slower query; all replicas down -> partial: true
embed queue lags  -> Kafka lag > 5 min           -> add embed GPUs; index labels/metadata first             -> new clips late in vector search only
bad label batch   -> reviewers overturn > 5%     -> stop that model version, superseding events; datasets stay pinned -> wrong labels ≤ 1 h
chose: shard by clip id · plan by selectivity · vectors+labels+filters in one shard · delta + immutable segments · versioned label events · hedge at shard p95 (15% of queries hit some p99) · trie rebuilt offline
```

[57-60 min · Summary, said not written.]{.rev-step}

"Search over a billion clips by text, example and metadata. 2.3 TB of vectors in RAM means 16 shards and a scatter-gather on every query inside 500 ms, so the design is a filter planner that picks post-filter, filtered traversal or exact scan by selectivity, immutable segments plus a small delta for minutes of freshness, and versioned label events so re-labeling never changes a dataset in flight."

<p class="rev-short">Shorthand used on the boards: WS = WebSocket · GW = gateway · KV = key-value store · TTL = time to live · idem = idempotency key · SSE = server-sent events · DLQ = dead-letter queue · P2P = peer-to-peer · 2PC = two-phase commit · CDC = change data capture · WFQ = weighted fair queuing · LWW = last-writer-wins register · HLC = hybrid logical clock · OT = operational transformation · RRF = reciprocal rank fusion · SFU = selective forwarding unit (the media server) · RTCP = the RTP control channel that reports media health · EC = erasure coding · AFR = annual disk failure rate · IOPS = disk operations per second · PFS = parallel file system · TSDB = time-series database.</p>

<p class="rev-actions"><button type="button" class="rev-drawn" data-for="b06-board">drawn today</button></p>

</div>
</details>

<details class="rev" data-card="b07-board" data-kind="do">
<summary><span class="rev-head"><span class="rev-tag">BOARD 07 · WHOLE BOARD</span><span class="rev-q">Reserve and dispatch GPU capacity for live streams: write the whole board on paper, scale first.</span></span></summary>
<div class="rev-a">

[0-8 min · Requirements, top-left]{.rev-step}

```text
FR   search free capacity by region + time, with price/slot · basket holds that expire · checkout: pay + confirm all or none
     dispatch a live stream to nearest pool with free units, reservation first · re-dispatch after pool/region failure · cancel with stated refund
NFR  never double book (except stated 10% overbooking) · search p99 < 300 ms, seconds stale ok · checkout < 2 s + bank call
     dispatch < 100 ms, 99.99% · booking = consistency over availability; dispatch = availability · re-place a failed region inside 60 s resume grace
OUT  GPU serving, model routing (board 2), spot market (board 8), invoicing, fraud
```

[8-13 min · Numbers, top-right]{.rev-step}

```text
unit = 1 live stream; 50 streams/GPU · 5 regions × 4 pools × 100 GPU × 50 = 100k units · slots 15 min -> 20 × 96 × 90 d = 172,800 rows ≈ 17 MB
bookings 100k/day = 1.2/s, 6/s peak -> 16 slot rows each ≈ 100 row writes/s · searches 1,000:1 -> 1,200/s, 6,000 peak
heartbeats 100k ÷ 4 s = 25k/s (Redis) · pool reports 20/s · dispatches 100k ÷ 600 s ≈ 170/s · sessions 100k × 200 B = 20 MB
region loss at 09:00: 20k units, 14k live at 70% -> re-place in 60 s; survivors 4 × 6k = 24k free
-> volume is trivial; the FAILURE case forces it: 14,000 streams moving in 60 s, and the free-unit margin across regions
```

[13-17 min · API, left]{.rev-step}

```text
GET  /capacity/search?region&start&end&units -> [{pool, slots [{slot, free, price}], quote_id (10 min)}]
POST /baskets/{id}/items {pool, start, end, units, quote_id} + Idempotency-Key -> {hold_id, expires_at, locked_price} · 409 if gone
POST /baskets/{id}/checkout {payment_token} + Idempotency-Key -> 202 {order_id, PENDING} -> CONFIRMED | FAILED (webhook/poll); all or none
POST /streams/dispatch {reservation_id | on_demand, device_region, model} -> {pool, gateway_url, token, lease_expires}; 429 + jittered Retry-After in storms
DELETE /reservations/{id} -> {refund}  (full > 24 h before, half after)
```

[17-21 min · Data, left under API]{.rev-step}

```text
slot(pool, slot_start): total, sellable (= units we may sell: total, or 1.1 × total where overbooking is allowed), reserved, held, version -> Postgres, one primary per region; conditional update = the guard
hold(hold_id; idx pool+slot): units, slots, expires_at, IN_CHECKOUT, fencing token -> same shard, same tx as slot rows
reservation(id): customer, pool, slots, units, status -> Postgres · basket(customer) -> DynamoDB + Redis write-through (cart)
idem(customer, key) -> Postgres UNIQUE · ledger(entry) -> Postgres append-only (Stripe)
pool_load(pool): free units, healthy, report_seq -> Redis per region, TTL 3 s · claims(pool, report_seq) -> Redis counter · session(session_id) -> Redis TTL 15 s
price_multiplier(pool, slot) -> Redis, rewritten each minute
```

[21-36 min · Diagram, center, in draw order]{.rev-step}

```text
1 customers/autoscalers -> API gateway (auth, rate limit) -> search service -> availability cache (CDC from Postgres) + pricer (surge per pool/slot)
2 gateway -> basket service -> basket store · basket -> reservation service (holds, checkout saga) -> Postgres per region -> CDC -> cache
3 reservation service -> payment gateway (idempotent charge, ledger) · -> lock manager (basket lease + fencing token at checkout)
4 devices -> regional dispatcher (pool table in RAM) -> Redis (pool load, claims, sessions) <- GPU pools report every 1 s · dispatcher -> Postgres (reservation check) · -> admission bucket (reconnects) -> gateway_url back to device
```

[36-52 min · Two deep dives, annotate the boxes]{.rev-step}

```text
A no double booking: (pool, slot) row = AirBnB's (listing, date) · hold = one conditional UPDATE: held += u WHERE sellable - reserved - held ≥ u, all 32 rows in slot order, one tx (~5 ms, ~200/s on the hottest row vs 6/s)
  any row fails -> rollback -> 409 · one region = one primary -> local tx; saga only across regions (hold A, hold B, release A on failure); no 2PC, a hold is already reversible
  checkout: lease on basket (lock manager), idem key, holds -> IN_CHECKOUT with expiry pushed past 2 min payment timeout + fencing token, order PENDING, COMMIT, then bank call
  expired holds swept every 10 s AND inline on guard failure · overbook 10% only where ≥ 20% idle history; failure -> nearest region, else 429 + 2× credit
  REJECT SELECT FOR UPDATE through checkout (2-5 s lock, pool drains); Redis as booking truth (not in the durable tx)
B dispatch under failure: regional dispatchers, static pool table + neighbor regions by latency; 20 pools need no geohash (Uber's lesson that survives: in-memory state with TTL)
  pools report free units each 1 s; 3 missed -> suspect, no new streams · its streams call resume -> same region first, then nearest neighbor; reserved first, spot shed
  admission 1,000 dispatches/s per region + client jitter 0-30 s -> 14k streams placed ~35 s after detection · survivors 24k free vs 14k -> overbooking STOPS on any degradation
  REJECT global dispatcher (cross-region RTT 50-150 ms breaks 100 ms; one failure for the fleet); instant reconnect (thundering herd)
```

[52-57 min · Failures and trade-offs, bottom]{.rev-step}

```text
region loses power 09:00 -> 3 missed reports, connections drop -> pools down, sellable -> 0, re-dispatch via admission, reserved first -> 5-35 s gap, +50-150 ms, auto credit
payment times out       -> PENDING > 2 min                    -> reconciler asks bank; retry with same key finds order          -> "processing", never charged twice
basket hoarding         -> hold age, units per customer       -> 10 min TTL, 2 extensions, 3 baskets, held ≤ 2× confirmed spend  -> "expired, re-check price"
chose: conditional update over row lock through checkout · saga+holds over 2PC · fenced lease only at checkout · TTL inline + sweeper · price shown with search · regional dispatchers · admission + jitter on resume
```

[57-60 min · Summary, said not written.]{.rev-step}

"A booking system for GPU stream capacity plus a dispatcher for live streams. Bookings are small, about 6 a second on 172,800 slot rows; the failure case is large, 14,000 live streams moving in 60 seconds. A conditional update on the pool-slot row is the only double-booking guard, holds protected through checkout carry the payment, and regional dispatchers with admission control and jitter absorb the reconnect storm, with overbooking that stops the moment a region degrades."

<p class="rev-short">Shorthand used on the boards: WS = WebSocket · GW = gateway · KV = key-value store · TTL = time to live · idem = idempotency key · SSE = server-sent events · DLQ = dead-letter queue · P2P = peer-to-peer · 2PC = two-phase commit · CDC = change data capture · WFQ = weighted fair queuing · LWW = last-writer-wins register · HLC = hybrid logical clock · OT = operational transformation · RRF = reciprocal rank fusion · SFU = selective forwarding unit (the media server) · RTCP = the RTP control channel that reports media health · EC = erasure coding · AFR = annual disk failure rate · IOPS = disk operations per second · PFS = parallel file system · TSDB = time-series database.</p>

<p class="rev-actions"><button type="button" class="rev-drawn" data-for="b07-board">drawn today</button></p>

</div>
</details>

<details class="rev" data-card="b08-board" data-kind="do">
<summary><span class="rev-head"><span class="rev-tag">BOARD 08 · WHOLE BOARD</span><span class="rev-q">Usage metering, quotas, and a spot auction for scarce GPU capacity: write the whole board on paper, scale first.</span></span></summary>
<div class="rev-a">

[0-8 min · Requirements, top-left]{.rev-step}

```text
FR   usage per key/org within seconds (dashboard) · quota enforcement within seconds · exact monthly invoice, each line traceable to raw events
     pace each org's daily budget evenly · per-minute auction per pool for surplus capacity, market data to bidders · auditable, replayable
NFR  ingest 10⁶ events/s, no back pressure on the API path · quota + dashboard freshness < 10 s p99
     each event billed exactly once · bid ack < 50 ms, clearing < 1 s after close · any minute's auction reproducible from its log for 400 days
OUT  gateway itself (board 2), GPU dispatch (board 7), tax/payments, fraud
```

[8-13 min · Numbers, top-right]{.rev-step}

```text
peak 10⁶ ev/s, avg ≈ 333k/s -> 2.9×10¹⁰/day · 500 B each -> 500 MB/s = 4 Gbps in · 100k keys, 10k orgs, biggest org 10%
Kafka: 10 MB/s per partition -> 50, take 256 (headroom, hot org) · 15 TB/day × 3 d × 3 copies = 135 TB -> 24 brokers × 8 TB
dedup ids 12 min TTL: 10⁶ × 720 × 16 B ≈ 11.5 GB (~20 GB in RocksDB), 80 MB per slot · real-time store 100k keys × 3 × 2 per 10 s = 60k writes/s (17× reduction)
raw Parquet 3 TB/day × 400 d = 1.2 PB · bids 10k/s vs exchange's 100k · market data 1 MB/s
-> 10⁶ events/s with ~20 GB of dedup state forces a stream processor; 72 h lateness forces a separate exact batch for billing; 10 s freshness forces early results
```

[13-17 min · API, left]{.rev-step}

```text
usage event -> Kafka: {event_id = idem_key + part, org, key, pool, model, metric: tokens|frames|gpu_ms, qty, event_time, producer}  acks=all, disk spool
GET  /usage?org&key&from&to&granularity=10s|1m|1h -> {series, as_of_watermark}
PUT  /budgets/{org} {daily_limit_usd, pacing: even|asap}
POST /spot/bids {pool, minute, units, max_price, client_order_id} -> 202 {bid_id, seq} · DELETE before close · WS market data {pool, minute, clearing_price, filled, depth (after close)}
GET  /invoices/{id}/lines/{line}/evidence -> {ledger_entry, batch_run_id, input_manifest, event_count, sample_ids}
```

[17-21 min · Data, left under API]{.rev-step}

```text
usage events(partition by org, shard)                    -> Kafka 256 partitions, 3 d · raw archive(date, org, event_id) -> object store Parquet 400 d
dedup set(event_id, TTL 12 min)                          -> processor RocksDB state, checkpointed with windows
real-time aggregate(key, metric, pool, window_start 10 s) -> Cassandra (SET, not increment) · series -> TSDB roll-ups
quota/pacing rates(key) -> rules store -> gateway RAM · daily spend(org, day) -> Redis SET to running total
ledger + invoice lines(org, day, metric, pool, batch_run) -> Postgres append-only, double-entry
sequenced bids(pool, seq) -> Kafka 1 partition per pool -> archive · order book(pool, minute) -> engine RAM · clearing(pool, minute) -> Postgres idempotent
```

[21-36 min · Diagram, center, in draw order]{.rev-step}

```text
1 gateways + workers -> Kafka (256 partitions by org+shard) -> stream processor (dedup, 10 s windows, early results, watermark 2 min)
2 processor -> Cassandra (aggregates) · -> TSDB (dashboards) · -> Redis (daily spend) · aggregates + spend -> pacing/quota controller (5 s) -> rate rules -> gateway RAM
3 Kafka -> object store (raw Parquet) -> batch job (hourly/nightly, exact) -> billing ledger -> invoicer (day 4) · batch -> reconciler (stream vs batch, 0.5%)
4 bidders -> sequencer (one log per pool, CLOSE marker) -> matching engine (one thread per pool) -> market data -> bidders · -> clearing results -> board 7 dispatcher · hot standby replays same log
```

[36-52 min · Two deep dives, annotate the boxes]{.rev-step}

```text
A exactly-once as an effect: at-least-once everywhere + stable id + idempotent writes · id = gateway idempotency key + part -> same id through gateway, meter, ledger
  dedup set per partition, 12 min TTL · 10 s tumbling event-time windows; early total every 10 s (dashboard, quotas), final when watermark (2 min) passes
  ≤ 10 min late -> window re-fires corrected total · later -> late topic, correction row · sink = SET per (key, metric, pool, window); crash -> checkpoint 30 s earlier, replay rewrites same values
  batch: no TTL, dedups the whole day, counts 72 h stragglers; ONLY batch writes the ledger · stream vs batch > 0.5% -> alert before invoice
  REJECT invoice from stream (12 min memory); central Redis SETNX per event (15-20 nodes + a hop per event)
B matching engine: pool = symbol · bids for m+1 open until sequencer writes CLOSE(m): cutoff is a seq number, not a clock -> primary and standby agree
  one thread per pool reads the log; book = tree by price desc, seq asc within price · supply = board 7 surplus forecast · fill from top, last fill partial
  uniform clearing price = highest REJECTED bid, reserve as floor -> truthful for 1-unit bidders, only reduces shading for multi-unit (say it) · publish fills, price, 1-min leases; result keyed (pool, minute) -> duplicate publish harmless
  REJECT continuous double auction (one seller, fastest bot wins); multi-threaded or DB-backed book (locks cost more than matching, no total order = no proof)
```

[52-57 min · Failures and trade-offs, bottom]{.rev-step}

```text
partition lags 5 min -> consumer lag, watermark age > 3 min (2 is normal) -> freeze rates for its keys; > 90% quota -> safe rate -> dashboard "as of 5 min ago", billing unaffected
engine host dies    -> missed heartbeats                            -> hot standby holds every bid from the log, clears on time -> nothing, or 1-2 s late
hot org skews       -> lag on one partition, 50 MB/s from one org   -> sub-partition (org, shard), merge in second stage        -> others keep 10 s freshness
chose: invoice from batch only · gateway idem key as event id · SET totals not increments · limiter local, controller rewrites rates · (org, shard) partitions · per-minute call auction, uniform price · one sequencer + one thread per pool
```

[57-60 min · Summary, said not written.]{.rev-step}

"Metering and a market on top of the API platform. A million events a second at 500 bytes is 4 Gbps and about 20 GB of de-duplication state, and events can be 72 hours late. Two paths over one log: a stream with 10-second windows and early results for quotas and dashboards, and an exact batch that alone writes the ledger. Exactly-once is an effect of the gateway's idempotency key as the event id plus idempotent window writes. One sequencer and one engine thread per pool clear a uniform price each minute, and replaying the log proves who came first."

<p class="rev-short">Shorthand used on the boards: WS = WebSocket · GW = gateway · KV = key-value store · TTL = time to live · idem = idempotency key · SSE = server-sent events · DLQ = dead-letter queue · P2P = peer-to-peer · 2PC = two-phase commit · CDC = change data capture · WFQ = weighted fair queuing · LWW = last-writer-wins register · HLC = hybrid logical clock · OT = operational transformation · RRF = reciprocal rank fusion · SFU = selective forwarding unit (the media server) · RTCP = the RTP control channel that reports media health · EC = erasure coding · AFR = annual disk failure rate · IOPS = disk operations per second · PFS = parallel file system · TSDB = time-series database.</p>

<details class="rev" data-card="b09-board" data-kind="do">
<summary><span class="rev-head"><span class="rev-tag">BOARD 09 · WHOLE BOARD</span><span class="rev-q">Model hub feed and recommendations for a research community: write the whole board on paper, scale first.</span></span></summary>
<div class="rev-a">

[0-8 min · Requirements, top-left]{.rev-step}

```text
FR   follow/unfollow models, datasets, teams, people · ranked home feed (versions, eval results, discussions)
     "you may want to follow" from the collaboration graph, with a reason · connection degree (1st/2nd/3rd) on every badge · typeahead over names
NFR  feed p99 < 200 ms · degree < 50 ms any pair · typeahead < 100 ms · new post in followers' feeds < 10 s, even from a 1M-follower model
     suggestions ≤ 24 h stale, minutes for a new connection · 99.9%, stale beats error
OUT  hosting model files, running evals, discussion threads, notifications, moderation
```

[8-13 min · Numbers, top-right]{.rev-step}

```text
5M users, 1M DAU · 170k followable things besides people (100k models, 50k datasets, 20k teams) · follows 5M × 50 = 2.5×10⁸ · collaboration edges 10⁸ · posts 100k/day = 1.2/s
degree badges 1M × 50 pages × 20 = 10⁹/day ≈ 11,500/s -> 58k peak · feed reads 1M × 20 = 230/s -> 1,200 peak · typeahead 580/s
fan-out (non-celebrity) 100k × 200 = 2×10⁷/day = 230/s · celebrity line 10k followers (~500 models, datasets or people above it) · 1M-follower push = 10⁶ writes (2-20 node-s), ×10 versions = 10⁷
hot: timelines 1M × 800 × 8 B = 6.4 GB · second-degree sets 3.2 GB · suggestions 6 GB · trie 1.6 GB · degree graph (collaborators + mutual follows) ≈ 6 GB -> fits every degree server
-> two numbers: 10⁶ writes per celebrity post (head-of-line blocking), and 58k degree reads/s on a graph small enough to replicate
```

[13-17 min · API, left]{.rev-step}

```text
GET  /feed?limit=20&cursor -> {items [{post_id, type, author, created_at, eval_delta, collapsed_count}], next_cursor}
POST /posts {author_entity, type: version|eval|discussion, body, version_ref} + Idempotency-Key -> 201 {post_id}  (fan-out async)
POST /follows {target_type, target_id} · DELETE  (publish follow event)
GET  /suggestions?limit=20 -> {items [{entity_id, reason "3 shared co-authors", score}]} · DELETE /suggestions/{id}
POST /degree/batch {target_ids[]} -> {u1: 1, u2: 2, u3: 3}  (one call per page of badges)
```

[17-21 min · Data, left under API]{.rev-step}

```text
post(post_id Snowflake; partition by author)                  -> Cassandra · post objects -> Memcached (multi-get)
follow(follower, followee) sharded by follower + follow_by_followee(followee, follower) sharded by followee -> Postgres (both sides)
degree adjacency(user -> neighbors: collaborators + mutual follows) -> KV, loaded into degree servers RAM (6 GB × 8)
timeline:{user} last 800 ids (14 d inactive expiry) · recent:{celebrity} last 100 -> Redis
suggestions:{user} sorted set -> Redis (Cassandra behind) · second_degree:{user} set or Bloom filter, TTL 24 h -> Redis
eval metrics(model, benchmark, version) -> time-series store, read with 30 ms timeout · trie snapshot hourly -> object store -> RAM
```

[21-36 min · Diagram, center, in draw order]{.rev-step}

```text
1 clients -> API gateway -> post service -> Cassandra; -> Kafka (post + follow events)
2 Kafka -> fan-out workers (push if author < 10k followers; read follow_by_followee) -> Redis timelines · celebrity -> recent:{author} only
3 gateway -> feed service (read timeline + pull 5 celeb lists via 2 s near cache, merge, collapse bursts, rank) -> Memcached posts, metrics store (timeout)
4 gateway -> follow service -> Postgres edges -> Kafka       5 gateway -> degree service (graph in RAM, 8 replicas) -> second-degree sets; KV adjacency -> degree service, Spark
6 job scheduler (nightly) -> Spark (2-hop, 3-hop, sampled co-follow) -> suggestion lists -> suggestion service (last-mile filter)     7 gateway -> typeahead servers (trie)
```

[36-52 min · Two deep dives, annotate the boxes]{.rev-step}

```text
A hybrid fan-out: push < 10k followers (deliberately 10× below Twitter's line; small Redis fleet), pull above · 10k push < 1 s; 1M = 10⁶ writes blocking the queue, ×10 versions = 10⁷
  ~500 celebrities, ~5 followed per user -> pull = one multi-get of 5 short lists per read (6k list reads/s at peak), near cache 2 s absorbs the hot key
  merge two sorted lists in memory at read; collapse 10 versions/day into one card with a count · timelines for active users only; rebuild on return by pull
  REJECT pure push (10⁷ writes, minutes of lag for everyone queued behind); pure pull (50 lists per read = 60k list reads/s, long p99)
B recommendation precompute: nightly Spark on a graph snapshot at 02:00; output keyed by snapshot date -> rerun overwrites · sources: collaborators², co-follow, same org
  collaborators 5M × 20² = 2×10⁹ pair votes; co-follow dominates -> sample 200 followers per entity -> 170k × 200² ≈ 7×10⁹; exclude entities > 10k followers (10¹² pairs); cap collaborators at 500 -> ~10¹⁰ total, a few hours
  3-hop only for users with < 5 two-hop candidates · top 100 per user = 6 GB into a new keyspace, switch once · follow event -> mini-update for both users in minutes
  cold start: org from email domain/SSO -> what colleagues follow; else trending in chosen topics; after 3 follows a per-user job · REJECT on-request (30k² pairs); random walks now (later, as degree grows)
```

[52-57 min · Failures and trade-offs, bottom]{.rev-step}

```text
1M-follower model posts 10 versions -> post rate per author, near-cache hit rate -> pull path, no fan-out; collapse -> one card "10 new versions"
recompute fails 2 nights            -> age of live keyspace > 26 h (not exit codes) -> serve last good lists; last-mile filter hides new follows -> up to 3 days stale, still valid
metrics store down                  -> 30 ms timeouts trip breaker              -> rank on recency/affinity/type, cards "eval pending"            -> slightly duller feed, never an error
chose: push < 10k / pull above · collapse bursts at read · nightly Spark + event mini-updates · exclude supernodes, sample followers · replicate 6 GB graph in RAM over sharding · metrics behind a timeout · hourly offline trie
```

[57-60 min · Summary, said not written.]{.rev-step}

"A social layer for a model hub: feed, follow suggestions, degree badges and typeahead for 5 million users following models, datasets, teams and people. Two numbers forced it: a million-follower post is a million timeline writes that block the queue, and degree badges run at 58,000 reads a second on a graph of only 6 gigabytes. So hybrid fan-out with bursts collapsed at read, nightly two-hop suggestions with supernodes excluded and event-driven mini-updates, and the whole degree graph in RAM on every degree server."

<p class="rev-short">Shorthand used on the boards: WS = WebSocket · GW = gateway · KV = key-value store · TTL = time to live · idem = idempotency key · SSE = server-sent events · DLQ = dead-letter queue · P2P = peer-to-peer · 2PC = two-phase commit · CDC = change data capture · WFQ = weighted fair queuing · LWW = last-writer-wins register · HLC = hybrid logical clock · OT = operational transformation · RRF = reciprocal rank fusion · SFU = selective forwarding unit (the media server) · RTCP = the RTP control channel that reports media health · EC = erasure coding · AFR = annual disk failure rate · IOPS = disk operations per second · PFS = parallel file system · TSDB = time-series database.</p>

<details class="rev" data-card="b10-board" data-kind="do">
<summary><span class="rev-head"><span class="rev-tag">BOARD 10 · WHOLE BOARD</span><span class="rev-q">Evaluation and testing harness for LLM coding agents: write the whole board on paper, diagram first.</span></span></summary>
<div class="rev-a">

[0-5 min · The agent loop (only if the first prompt is "Build a coding agent", otherwise these minutes go to requirements)]{.rev-step}

```text
LOOP     user msg -> context = system prompt + tool schemas + history -> model call (streamed)
         -> tool_use? -> permission check (allow / ask / deny, per tool and per path) -> run tool -> append tool_result -> loop
         -> stop on a final answer, max turns, or user interrupt
TOOLS    read / write / edit file · shell command (compiler, tests) in a sandbox · code search (grep, glob, symbol index) · web fetch
CONTEXT  stable prefix cached (system + tools) · compaction near the window limit: summarize old turns, keep plan + files touched
SESSION  every event appended to a server-side session log (same schema as the harness trajectory)
         laptop -> phone = a thin client reattaches by session_id and tails the live log (Kafka or a hot store) from its last seq
MEDIA    images / audio in -> upload -> file_id in the message · out: text, diffs, Mermaid or image diagrams
```

[5-10 min · Requirements, top-left (accept what is dictated, compress, move)]{.rev-step}

```text
FR   run a suite: N tasks x agent build x model version -> k samples per task, each try in its own fresh sandbox
     tools against the sandbox: files, shell, compiler and test output, code search · multimodal task inputs
     score each sample: hidden unit tests, compile, LLM judge · compare run A vs run B per task, same suite version
     record the full trajectory (model calls, tool calls, outputs, latency) · replay and debug any try
NFR  one release run = 10,000 agents x up to 100 turns, done in < 30 min (task in -> final score)
     no state survives between tries · deterministic where we control it · control plane 99.99%
     99.99% = Postgres sync replica across 3 AZs · scheduler leader election · Kafka RF 3 · hosts across 3 AZs
     keep everything for replay · hot 30 days, then cold
OUT  model serving, weights, inference engine, GPUs, cost (declared infinite)
```

[10-24 min · Diagram, center, in draw order]{.rev-step}

```text
1 UI / CI -> API (auth, idem) -> Postgres (run, samples expanded from the suite)
2 scheduler -> lease try with epoch -> sandbox host · all 10,000 start in a 30 s ramp
3 host: restore microVM = base snapshot (toolchain hash) + task disk layer (content hash, lazy copy-on-write) -> workspace only
  runner + tool broker run OUTSIDE the SBX on the host · tools exec in the SBX over vsock
4 runner -> model GW (least-slack-first, retries, per-run quota) -> model API · SBX egress = frozen package mirror only
5 runner -> event log (append, seq, epoch) -> object storage (Parquet + blobs) and ClickHouse
6 final answer -> runner exports diff -> object storage · scheduler starts evaluator in a FRESH SBX
  evaluator: apply diff, restore hidden tests + protected paths, flag a diff that touches them -> tests, compile, LLM judge -> scores
7 destroy SBX, host checks no VMM process, tap device or disk layer outlives the lease
8 replay service: render from the log, or re-execute in a new SBX · results UI queries ClickHouse + scores
```

[24-26 min · One line of numbers, top-right]{.rev-step}

```text
10^4 agents x 100 turns (cap) = 10^6 turns · natural 10^4 / 10 s per turn ≈ 1,000 calls/s · floor 10^6 / 1,500 s ≈ 670/s (25-min cap)
quota ask ≈ 1,000 calls/s x 30k tokens ≈ 2x10^9 TPM · 15 s per turn at the cap, model p50 5-10 s, so queues stay near empty
storage 10^6 turns x 20 KB = 20 GB events + 10 GB artifacts ≈ 30 GB/run · 30 GB / 1,800 s ≈ 17 MB/s, small
```

[26-32 min · API and data, left]{.rev-step}

```text
POST /v1/suites {tasks: [{repo_snapshot, prompt, inputs: file_ids, hidden_tests, protected_paths, timeout}]} -> {suite_id, version} (immutable)
POST /v1/runs {suite_id@version, agent_build_hash, model_version, samples_per_task, seed} + Idempotency-Key -> 202 {run_id}
GET  /v1/runs/{id} -> {state, done, passed, failed, timed_out, infra}   · POST /v1/runs/{id}:cancel (CANCELLING, CANCELLED)
GET  /v1/runs/{a}/compare/{b} (409 if suite versions differ) · GET /v1/tries/{id}/events?from_seq · POST .../replay {mode}
run (run_id): pins suite version, agent build, model version, image hash, mirror snapshot -> Postgres
sample (run_id, task_id, sample_no) · try (sample_id, try_no): host, lease_epoch, lease_until, state -> Postgres
event (attempt_id, try_no, seq): type, payload <= 4 KB or blob hash, content_hash -> Kafka -> Parquet (truth) + ClickHouse
artifact, score (attempt_id, evaluator, evaluator_version) -> object storage, Postgres
```

[32-48 min · Two deep dives, annotate the boxes]{.rev-step}

```text
A isolation + determinism: fresh microVM per try, workspace only · runner and credentials outside · egress = frozen mirror
  pinned toolchain hash, mirror snapshot, repo commit · fixed seed, clock set at boot · destroy at end · host leak checks
  limits: the clock moves after boot, parallel test order, thread scheduling, so tool outputs are recorded, never assumed
  REJECT reused containers with cleanup (caches, /tmp, background processes leak) · REJECT live internet (non-reproducible)
B trajectory + replay: event = (attempt_id, try_no, seq, type, payload or blob hash, content_hash), append-only, deltas
  replay 1 render: read the log, no compute
  replay 2 re-execute: new SBX, model responses served from the log by request hash, tools run for real
    outputs normalized (durations, PIDs, temp paths stripped) before hashing · divergence = first seq whose normalized hash differs
  replay 3 agent-only: recorded tool results too, fully deterministic, for testing a new agent build
  retention hot 30 d / cold 1 yr · task code can be customer code: encrypted, access-logged, never in the analytics rows
```

[48-55 min · Failures and trade-offs, bottom]{.rev-step}

```text
stuck agent      tool call > 90 s or model call > 60 s · no event 120 s · attempt > 25 min   kill, TIMED_OUT (agent fault, scored fail)
sandbox leak     lease without heartbeat · VMM process, tap device or disk layer outlives lease   reaper destroys, host drained after 3 leaks
model GW 429     429 rate, queue time per turn          backoff + jitter, least-slack-first, short quota: stratified sample, run PARTIAL
poison task      same task fails INFRA 3 times across hosts                                       quarantine, report, run finishes
scheduler crash  leader lease lost    new leader · hosts renew try leases in Postgres · re-lease bumps epoch, stale epoch writes rejected
chose: runner outside SBX · microVM per try · admission to quota · record model + tool outputs · log is truth · INFRA != agent failure
```

[55-60 min · Summary, said not written.]{.rev-step}

"A run is 10,000 samples. Each try gets a fresh microVM workspace restored from a pinned snapshot, while the agent runner stays outside it on the host with the credentials. Every model call and tool call is an append-only event with a sequence number and a content hash, so any try can be re-rendered exactly, or re-executed against its recorded model responses until the first normalized divergence. The 30-minute budget is a per-turn latency budget: up to 100 sequential turns in 25 minutes, so the gateway serves the least-slack agent first and the quota is sized to the natural rate, not the average."

<p class="rev-short">Shorthand used on this board: SBX = sandbox (one microVM, workspace only) · runner = the trusted agent runner on the host · GW = gateway · idem = idempotency key · seq = per-try event sequence number · epoch = lease fencing token · INFRA = infra error, not the agent's fault · TPM = tokens per minute · p50 = median latency · LLM judge = a model that grades an output against a rubric.</p>

<p class="rev-actions"><button type="button" class="rev-drawn" data-for="b10-board">drawn today</button></p>

</div>
</details>

<summary><span class="rev-head"><span class="rev-tag">BOARD 10 · NUMBERS</span><span class="rev-q">Evaluation and testing harness for LLM coding agents: the numbers block (24-26 min).</span></span></summary>
<div class="rev-a">

```text
10^4 agents x 100 turns (cap) = 10^6 turns · natural 10^4 / 10 s per turn ≈ 1,000 calls/s · floor 10^6 / 1,500 s ≈ 670/s (25-min cap)
quota ask ≈ 1,000 calls/s x 30k tokens ≈ 2x10^9 TPM · 15 s per turn at the cap, model p50 5-10 s, so queues stay near empty
storage 10^6 turns x 20 KB = 20 GB events + 10 GB artifacts ≈ 30 GB/run · 30 GB / 1,800 s ≈ 17 MB/s, small
```

<summary><span class="rev-head"><span class="rev-tag">BOARD 10 · DIAGRAM</span><span class="rev-q">Evaluation and testing harness for LLM coding agents: the diagram in draw order (10-24 min).</span></span></summary>
<div class="rev-a">

```text
1 UI / CI -> API (auth, idem) -> Postgres (run, samples expanded from the suite)
2 scheduler -> lease try with epoch -> sandbox host · all 10,000 start in a 30 s ramp
3 host: restore microVM = base snapshot (toolchain hash) + task disk layer (content hash, lazy copy-on-write) -> workspace only
  runner + tool broker run OUTSIDE the SBX on the host · tools exec in the SBX over vsock
4 runner -> model GW (least-slack-first, retries, per-run quota) -> model API · SBX egress = frozen package mirror only
5 runner -> event log (append, seq, epoch) -> object storage (Parquet + blobs) and ClickHouse
6 final answer -> runner exports diff -> object storage · scheduler starts evaluator in a FRESH SBX
  evaluator: apply diff, restore hidden tests + protected paths, flag a diff that touches them -> tests, compile, LLM judge -> scores
7 destroy SBX, host checks no VMM process, tap device or disk layer outlives the lease
8 replay service: render from the log, or re-execute in a new SBX · results UI queries ClickHouse + scores
```
